decisions.reason: Selecting Inter for article body typography does not change the requirement to break up long text with images, blurbs, or quotes.

Although font adjustment was previously considered as one possible whitespace remedy, the candidate's current methods are Fun Fact images for this issue and word-count guidance for the next; accepting Inter does not necessarily change either method or the ending standard.
The body-typeface selection does not alter author-name or author-photo presentation requirements.
The Inter selection does not change the requirement for correct table-of-contents page references after pagination is finalized.
The client accepts Inter for article body text but does not revise the broader polished, modern, brand-aligned visual-style requirement or its red-color rule.
Changing the article body typeface has no necessary effect on advertisement rendering clarity.
Inter was recommended partly for flipbook readability, but its acceptance does not change the candidate's deliverable or two-page-spread balance requirements.
The body-typeface choice does not add, remove, or otherwise change required issue content.
The source accepts a body typeface and does not revise article order, placement rules, or the flat-plan basis.
The body-typeface selection does not change the requirement to enhance image quality when needed.
The source contains no change to the digital launch target or deadline.
